To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) ensembles of classifiers are a promising approach for classification; 2) the best performance is obtained when using a combination of classifiers with different learning algorithms, which are trained on different subsets of the training set; 3) the best performance can be achieved by combining a large number of weak classifiers; and 4) the performance of the ensemble of classifiers can be improved by using different voting rules.

(1) The most accurate classifier in our experiments was the C4.5 decision tree, followed by Naive Bayes and the k-Nearest Neighbour classifier, with the Random Forest ensemble performing best among ensembles; (2) The best performance was achieved when all classifiers were trained and tested using the same data, and the same set of features, with the exception of the Naive Bayes classifier which performed best when the training set was augmented with the testing set.
the best performance is obtained by combining the results of the different algorithms and that the best results are obtained when using a large number of algorithms.
